evidence.claim: Buhari urged Nigerians to settle grievances peacefully, called on aspirants to avoid hate speech and divisive tendencies, and said violence generally mars elections.
evidence.title: Independence Day Address By President Buhari On Nigeria's 62nd Independence Anniversary Celebration
evidence.excerpt: Buhari urged Nigerians to settle grievances peacefully, called on aspirants to avoid hate speech and divisive tendencies, and said violence generally mars elections.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential speech with explicit anti-incitement and anti-violence language.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Buhari, though it is rhetoric rather than an operational security order.
contrary_evidence: Rhetoric alone does not show actual protection outcomes.
The address is self-presenting and may overstate government success.

evidence.claim: Buhari directed the armed forces to remain apolitical, improve human-rights obligations, and support a peaceful environment for the 2023 general elections.
evidence.title: President Buhari Canvasses Army Neutrality On 2023 Polls, Wants Human Rights Obligations Sustained
evidence.excerpt: Buhari directed the armed forces to remain apolitical, improve human-rights obligations, and support a peaceful environment for the 2023 general elections.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential instruction on a dated State House page.
evidence.period_fit: Late-2022 ruler conduct with direct domestic-safety relevance
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Buhari as commander-in-chief and relevant to civilian protection.
contrary_evidence: This is forward-looking guidance, not a proven outcome.
The speech is aimed at elections rather than everyday policing.

evidence.claim: SERAP went to court to force publication of the Twitter agreement because it feared the terms could jeopardize freedom of expression, and the government had suspended Twitter after Buhari's tweet was deleted.
evidence.title: Rights group goes to court to get Nigeria to publish agreement with Twitter
evidence.excerpt: SERAP went to court to force publication of the Twitter agreement because it feared the terms could jeopardize freedom of expression, and the government had suspended Twitter after Buhari's tweet was deleted.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters report on contemporaneous legal challenge and government position, with specific references to Buhari's tweet and the suspension.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Buhari's administration and information ministry, though not necessarily to Buhari's personal day-to-day direction.
contrary_evidence: Twitter had been restored by the time of the report, so the ban was not continuously in force in 2022.
This is a legal dispute over speech controls, not a physical-violence incident.

evidence.claim: Buhari signed the Electoral Act 2022, and the presidential release says it was intended to limit money politics and incumbent advantage, while being drafted with civil society, labor, media, and INEC consultation.
evidence.title: Assent Into Law of the Electoral Act 2022: Landmark Moment for the Nation
evidence.excerpt: Buhari signed the Electoral Act 2022, and the presidential release says it was intended to limit money politics and incumbent advantage, while being drafted with civil society, labor, media, and INEC consultation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential release about a dated legal act and its stated purpose.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Buhari as president and signer of the law.
contrary_evidence: This is an official self-description of the reform, so implementation quality is not proven here.
A law can improve rules without eliminating practical manipulation.

evidence.claim: Buhari said it was his last Democracy Day speech, promised a peaceful and transparent transfer to a new president in 2023, praised 2022 party primaries as peaceful and orderly, and said aggrieved actors sought judicial justice rather than violence.
evidence.title: President Buhari’s Democracy Day Speech
evidence.excerpt: Buhari said it was his last Democracy Day speech, promised a peaceful and transparent transfer to a new president in 2023, praised 2022 party primaries as peaceful and orderly, and said aggrieved actors sought judicial justice rather than violence.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential speech with explicit transition and contestability language.
contrary_evidence: This is rhetoric and self-presentation, not proof of actual electoral conduct.
The speech does not by itself rule out manipulation elsewhere in the system.

evidence.claim: Buhari said the 2023 elections would be free, fair, and credible, that manipulations would not be allowed, that people should vote for whoever they wanted, and that money and thugs would not be allowed to intimidate voters; the mission leader also praised him for not pursuing a third term.
evidence.title: President Buhari to West African Elders: Our Election Will be Free, Fair, Credible
evidence.excerpt: Buhari said the 2023 elections would be free, fair, and credible, that manipulations would not be allowed, that people should vote for whoever they wanted, and that money and thugs would not be allowed to intimidate voters; the mission leader also praised him for not pursuing a third term.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential statement, plus contemporaneous third-party commendation on the same page.
evidence.period_fit: late 2022, directly relevant to the 2023 transition prepared during 2022
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Buhari, with the third-term point coming from the visiting mission leader's statement.
contrary_evidence: The passage is aspirational and not a post-election audit.
The mission leader's praise is still not an independent election observation report.

evidence.claim: Buhari said the APC convention should promote internal democracy, respect the wishes of the people, de-emphasize money politics, resist the imposition of candidates, and allow popular aspirants to fly the party flag.
evidence.title: President Buharis’ Address at the APC National Convention
evidence.excerpt: Buhari said the APC convention should promote internal democracy, respect the wishes of the people, de-emphasize money politics, resist the imposition of candidates, and allow popular aspirants to fly the party flag.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential remarks at a dated party convention with explicit anti-imposition language.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Buhari in his role as APC leader and president.
contrary_evidence: This is a party speech, not a broader state reform assessment.
It shows declared preference for internal democracy, not guaranteed compliance.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Buhari, who was constitutionally barred from contesting, would step down in 2023 after eight years and had told APC governors that he had no preferred candidate and had anointed no one.
evidence.title: Nigeria: Buhari has no preferred successor, spokesman says
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Buhari, who was constitutionally barred from contesting, would step down in 2023 after eight years and had told APC governors that he had no preferred candidate and had anointed no one.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting with direct attribution and clear constitutional context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State-level succession behavior under Buhari, with the quote relayed through his spokesman.
contrary_evidence: Reuters reports a spokesperson's account, not a transcript of Buhari's own words.
No preferred successor does not prove complete neutrality in internal party competition.

evidence.claim: VOA Hausa reported Buhari warning the APC that lack of unity and selfishness could cost it the 2023 election, framing internal democracy and coalition discipline as necessary for success.
evidence.title: Shugaba Buhari Ya Gargadi Jam'iyyar APC Kan Hadin Kai
evidence.excerpt: VOA Hausa reported Buhari warning the APC that lack of unity and selfishness could cost it the 2023 election, framing internal democracy and coalition discipline as necessary for success.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs and quoted broadcast summary
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Local-language reporting with direct attribution to Buhari's televised remarks, but via a news summary rather than full transcript.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Buhari as APC leader and president.
contrary_evidence: This is a party-management warning, not proof of broader democratic liberalism.
It does not show treatment of opposition parties outside APC.

evidence.claim: VOA Hausa reported Buhari saying Nigeria would conduct an election acceptable to all candidates and voters, and that recent elections had shown improving democratic practice.
evidence.title: Za Mu Gudanar Da Zaben Da Kowa Zai Amince Da Shi - Buhari
evidence.excerpt: VOA Hausa reported Buhari saying Nigeria would conduct an election acceptable to all candidates and voters, and that recent elections had shown improving democratic practice.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Local-language reporting on direct Buhari remarks, with translation-dependent wording.
contrary_evidence: This is campaign-season rhetoric and not an election audit.
The statement is prospective and self-affirming.

unresolved_gaps: No direct 2022 Buhari decision on nuclear brinkmanship, command-and-control, or other existential-risk use of presidential authority.
No independent audit of whether the 2021-2022 safeguards and physical-protection framework was actually implemented in practice.
No direct evidence of Buhari personally directing external military operations, proxy conduct, or coercive cross-border action in 2022.
No substantive mediation track or concrete ceasefire result led by Buhari himself.
Independent, case-level follow-through on prosecutions and investigations for major 2022 abuses is thin.
Some severe insecurity items are still better understood as state failure in a violent environment than as direct ruler-directed violence.
No independent pre-election audit of how fully the Electoral Act 2022 was implemented before the 2023 polls.
Much of the affirmative evidence is self-description from Buhari and his administration.
Budget execution and capital-spending delivery are not independently audited at the project level here.
Household-level and regional distributional causality remains only partially evidenced.
Independent audit evidence on how much of the announced welfare and health delivery actually reached beneficiaries in 2022 is limited.
The chapter still mixes federal action, donor support, and inherited deprivation.
No direct 2022 evidence of Buhari's assets, procurement benefits, bribes, or formal audit/court findings tied to personal enrichment.
The family-appointment case is strong on patronage but still thin on Buhari's knowledge, benefit, and intent beyond approval.
The Lake Chad arms claim is shown as unsupported, but there is no public correction or retraction by Buhari in the package.
Independent audit-grade evidence on the delivery tracker and the administration's correction of weak implementers is still limited.
The chapter still depends heavily on macro outcomes that mix Buhari-era policy with inherited constraints and external shocks.
